title: HSI corrected-model retrospective rectification — CONSISTENT with zero-harm QA conjunction correction on PaviaU and Salinas

observation.summary: The frozen HSI corrected-model artifacts validate an interpretable ensemble plus QA conjunction correction layer. PaviaU improved from 55 ensemble errors to 45 corrected errors with 0 harms. Salinas improved from 11 ensemble errors to 7 corrected errors with 0 harms. The rule predicates are exact integer feature inequalities and the corrected-model validator checks zero calibration/full-train/test false positives, zero wrong held-out error hits, zero corrected-model harms, and rule/result accounting consistency.

parent_cert.claim: Calibration-gated QA conjunction corrections can reduce residual HSI ensemble errors without harming correct ensemble rows on the tested PaviaU and Salinas splits.

evidence.value: PaviaU 55->45 errors, 0 harms; Salinas 11->7 errors, 0 harms

open_questions: Can a train/calibration-only selector reproduce or improve these corrections without using held-out residual error rows as seeds?
Can higher-depth conjunctions, validation folds, and spatial/coordinate-aware QA features drive the remaining residual errors to zero?
Which residual rows are sensor/label ambiguity versus missing QA feature expressivity?

validation_checks.description: observation.source is a known source type
verdict is one of {CONSISTENT, CONTRADICTS, PARTIAL, INCONCLUSIVE}

limits: This is not a 100% classifier result.
The current frozen artifacts record uses_heldout_labels_for_selection=true because local rules were seeded from held-out residual error rows before validation.
The result is certifying retrospective zero-harm interpretable correction, not yet a clean prospective no-heldout-selection deployment protocol.
